page.notes: Marginal note "Patiens" stands beside the line "materialis, qui etiam possibilis" (second line of section II), and "Adeptus." beside the line "gat cum agente, dicitur intellectus adeptus." Both are inside the paragraph starting "II. Unus idemq;" and are placed at their printed positions in the left margin. The marginal words "Patiens" and "Adeptus." are not separately marked in the text, as they have no reference mark. "(five partes)": the printed word looks like "five", probably a misprint for "sive"; kept as printed. "exer.307.§8": the mark after 307 is a section sign, read with doubt. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout (e.g. "constitutus", "est"). Italic boundaries in section II are approximate. The last line ends with a printed hyphen ("sci-"), so the paragraph continues on the next page.
